And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

Cardiff City vs NorwichDoncaster Rovers vs MiddlesbroughBarnsley vs Crewe AlexandraBlackburn Rovers vs Sheffield UnitedBlackpool vs Lincoln CityCambridge United vs MillwallFleetwood Town vs Shrewsbury TownIpswich Town vs Leicester CityPlymouth vs Coventry CitySheffield Wednesday vs Wolverhampton WanderersSouthampton vs West Ham United Stevenage Town vs ReadingStoke City vs Hull City Walsall vs Leyton OrientWatford Peterborough UnitedBirmingham City vs BrentfordNottingham Forest vs Leeds United

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1456. Roma set new record for fastest brace at Old Trafford

Roma made history at Old Trafford. Thanks to goals from Soulé and Malen, which came in the first 18 minutes of the match against Manchester United, the Giallorossi set a new record at the English stadium.

Never before had a visiting team managed to score twice so early at Old Trafford in a major European match. Gasperini’s team broke the deadlock in the 11th minute through Soulé, before doubling their lead from the penalty spot seven minutes later through Malen.

This figure applies to all major European competitions played by Manchester United at their home ground, which has never before seen the visiting team score two goals in 17 minutes of play.

This start takes on even greater significance given the teams’ history. Roma had lost all four of their previous meetings at Old Trafford between 2007 and 2021.

#1455. Gasperini analyzes loss to Man United: “It teaches us a lot.”

A terrible late defeat condemned Roma to the Champions League.

Leading the way, the Giallorossi saw Manchester United overturn their lead in the final minutes: first a penalty from Bruno Fernandes, then a brace from Matheus Cunha.

The Brazilian first leveled the scoreline with a mistake from Balerdi, then scored the winner in the 86th minute, capping his wild night with a red card in the 91st.

After the match, Gian Piero Gasperini analyzed the painful defeat to Sky Sport, starting with the episode that changed the match’s momentum: “I think it was a different game than the one against Real Madrid,” the Giallorossi coach explained. “There weren’t such obvious signs of a decline, as there were after the penalty, which gave them a great boost.”

No excuses, however, for the inability to stem the Red Devils’ final assault: “There’s no coincidence in the goals we conceded in the comeback; tonight we didn’t have the strength to defend their attackers. It’s natural that you can struggle against Manchester United in the final 15 minutes if they attack like that.”

“They started to press further forward; we had to play differently, taking advantage of long balls. We weren’t able to keep up with them: we should have resorted to a few more tackles, but instead we suffered their momentum, which was amplified by the penalty and the 2-2 incident.”

On managing the right flank and using Lulli in place of the injured Rensch (with Molina left out): “Molina could have stayed in, yes. Rensch started well, then he got injured and I opted for Lulli. But that’s not the reason for the defeat. I think it was a different match, which taught us more than the one against Real Madrid.” He concluded by focusing on the psychological aspect of dealing with the backlash: “There was a bit of disappointment after seeing victory slip away from you at the front. The team perhaps needs to relieve itself of the pressure of a result at all costs.”

#1453. Cristante: “We cannot allow these comebacks. We need to revisit our mistakes.”

Bryan Cristante spoke to Sky Sport after the defeat against Manchester United.

“We came in well, we played a great first half that could have ended even more than 2-0. Then there are the opponents, who are strong and when they push forward and find the right moment, they become difficult to contain.”

“We had to do something more, especially because we’d been through it before. That penalty… I didn’t watch it again, but from the pitch it looked very dubious.”

“When they get going, they’re strong players and difficult to contain. We need to take a good look at it and understand where we’re going wrong; it’s becoming a bit too frequent.”

“We definitely need to be more focused at the back, the whole team. We were 2-0 up, and every now and then we can drop back and keep the game going, letting the others play, but without conceding goals. We need to revisit it and understand where we went wrong.”

“We played a great half, against a strong team despite not being in their best form, and in a stadium like this. We need to take the positives, but we know this is a point and we need to improve. We will do it, we need to understand where we went wrong so we don’t make these mistakes again.”

#1451. Carrick: “Roma are a great team, it was always going to be difficult.”

Following United’s 3-2 comeback win, Red Devils manager Michael Carrick spoke at a press conference analyzing the match against Roma.

“I’m really proud of my players; they deserve great respect for being able to turn the game around. The fans also did their part; they wanted to inspire us, and their support was palpable.”

“After the first half, there was a lot of frustration, but in the locker room, I reminded the boys how important the fans were. In the second half, we maintained a positive attitude and continued to believe until the end. It’s still a victory, nothing more.”

“It’s certainly a very significant result. Some players experienced sensations they hadn’t yet experienced at Old Trafford, and for the new arrivals, it was crucial to feel the support of the fans. Sometimes, it’s not easy to figure out how to overcome difficulties. Now, however, we must stay calm and focus on the next match.”

“We weren’t in an easy situation. Roma are a top-notch team, they marked the entire pitch individually, and we knew it would be a tough match. We left our opponents too much space, but gradually we managed to get closer to their goal. We knew they could cause us problems, but in those moments you have to keep believing in what you’re doing, without giving in to frustration.”

“In the first half, we could have lost confidence, especially after what happened to Bruno Fernandes on the penalty and Baleba’s exit. Tielemans made a good impact coming off the bench. We wanted to give this victory to our fans.”

#1449. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

It is all over in north London and Tottenham have booked their place in the third round of the League Cup with a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton.

Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

The Brazilian signed just yesterday but he now has a first Tottenham goal to his name. He cuts inside from the right and drives across the face of the penalty area before firing at the near post, beating Brooks. Tottenham are cruising into the third round and their newest signing scores on his debut.

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Tottenham are cruising into the third round and so are Everton, who lead Preston by the same scoreline. Newcastle lead West Brom 3-2 whilst it is still 0-0 between Bradford and Burnley.

Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

Tel crosses from the left side of the box and picks out Savio, who attempts an audacious flick that does not come off.

West Brom were not back on level terms for long as Barnes has his second of the game and Newcastle lead 3-2 with under 10 minutes remaining.

Charlton have barely threatened the Tottenham goal tonight but that is a decent opportunity for Leaburn, who is played in down the right and forces Kinsky into a decent save.

Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

Newcastle had fought from 1-0 down against West Brom to lead 2-1 but Hall has just given away a penalty for the second time in a matter of days having also conceded one in the dying moments of their 2-2 draw against Liverpool on Sunday. Price has stepped up to score his second of the game to bring West Brom level at 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go.

The Austrian defender has just come on and, with his first touch, puts Tottenham 3-0 up. Fernandes’ free-kick from just outside the box on the right is met by Danso, who attacks it and his header finds the bottom corner. You have to say that goal was coming. Danso has hurt himself as there was a clash of heads as he met the delivery and receives treatment to his head.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

Roberto De Zerbi is turning to his bench and making a triple change as Van de Ven, Danso and Porro come on.

Charlton are also making a triple change of their own.

Gray is found on the left side of the Charlton penalty area and he drives his shot towards goal, forcing Brooks into a decent save. Tottenham are pushing for that third goal.

A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

One of the new laws brought in this season is to speed up throw-ins and Gray falls foul of taking too long, with Charlton then being given the throw-in.

Tel decides to shoot from range after Charlton clear a corner but the Frenchman’s effort is straight at Brooks

Play has resumed in north London, with Tottenham 2-0 up over Charlton.

They are back under way at St James’ Park and there has been a goal within a few minutes of the second half starting. Newcastle were 1-0 down against West Brom but they now lead 2-1 thanks to Barnes’ goal.

The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

Tottenham are currently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball quickly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

That probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1442. Michael Carrick is the latest Man Utd boss to save his job with one result

Michael Carrick may have saved his Manchester United job after they overcame a 2-0 deficit to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.

For the first time since early September, United fans can celebrate a win and it is a result that may have saved Carrick’s job, for now.

Here are four other times United managers were given a stay of execution by a single result.

It’s the example that gets brought up every time a current Manchester United manager is struggling.

Ferguson was three years into his Manchester United tenure and things were not going so well.

A second-place finish was sandwiched between two 11th-place finishes; they would end the 1989-90 season in 13th and general consensus was Ferguson was not long for the sack.

It was a season which had seen United lose 5-1 away at their noisy neighbours. In December, a banner was unfurled, reading “3 Years Of Excuses And It’s Still Crap. Ta Ra Fergie”. Calls for the sack were growing by the day.

But it was the FA Cup that rescued the future great. United were away at Nottingham Forest in the third round and there was the hope that going on an elongated cup run may distract the Old Trafford faithful from the league form.

Their opponents were Brian Clough’s Forest, a fading giant but still a club that won two European Cups within recent memory. Ferguson made a selection gamble, playing 20-year-old striker Mark Robins and it worked.

The future Coventry manager grabbed the only goal of the game to put United through. They would go on to win the tournament and give Ferguson some much-needed breathing room.

That goal kickstarted the era that would see every trophy come to Old Trafford. United finished sixth the following season. The year after that they were second before winning the first Premier League season in 1993.

Carrick’s success is not the first time United have overcome a 2-0 deficit in Europe to save a manager’s job.

United had started the 2021-22 season poorly under Solskjaer. They had been knocked out of the League Cup. They had been beaten by Young Boys in the Champions League. They had won just one of their past five games and had most recently been thumped 4-2 by Leicester.

The boos that rang out at Old Trafford following a 1-1 draw at Everton showed that the usually patient home fans had turned on their 1999 hero.

And then Solskjaer’s P45 was practically being written up when United trailed Atalanta 2-0 after half an hour.

But a second-half comeback finished off by Cristiano Ronaldo gave Solskjaer a stay of execution, if only for a little while.

They lost the next game 5-0 to Liverpool but persevered with Solskjaer, who took them to second.

He was sacked after a 4-1 defeat at Watford in November.

By all reports, United were ready to sack Ten Hag that evening before he unexpectedly beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final.

United were rank outsiders when facing Pep Guardiola’s City, who had just won their fourth consecutive Premier League title, and yet saved their performance of the season for their final match of the season.

Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring on the half-hour mark before Kobbie Mainoo made it two nine minutes later. Ten Hag had outthought Pep, allowing City to have the ball before countering at pace. Jeremy Doku got one back but it was not enough to stop United winning their 13th FA Cup.

It was a moment that many hoped would parallel Ferguson, perhaps this could be what changed United’s fortunes. It wasn’t.

Ten Hag had finished eighth with them but widespread reports of his sacking had undermined any credibility the Dutchman had at the club.

Ten Hag had also given the green light to some of the worst signings in United history, particularly the £86 million paid to Ajax for Antony.

He was eventually sacked in October, just five months after the FA Cup win and delaying the decision cost United even more. Ruben Amorim, a man with a completely different system, was brought in mid-season and never recovered.

A League Cup exit at the hands of Derby and a 3-1 defeat to West Ham had Mourinho on the brink at United.

It was typical late-stage Mourinho. He had fallen out with a number of his own players, most notably Paul Pogba, and there was a cloud of toxicity suffocating the club.

When United went 2-0 down inside the opening 10 minutes against Newcastle at home, that looked to be the end of it.

But United woke up 20 minutes before time. Juan Mata, the much-maligned player under Mourinho at two successive clubs, had curled in a free kick. Anthony Martial equalised in the 76th minute.

And then Alexis Sanchez scored a dramatic late winner to give United the win and complete the comeback.

The fans cheered Mourinho’s name, but it only delayed the end rather than stopping it outright.

United drew the next game 2-2 to Chelsea but went on a run that saw them lose to Juventus, City and Liverpool. That 3-1 defeat at Anfield was enough for Mourinho to be given his marching orders.

#1441. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

#1440. Recalling Luis Figo’s stint at Inter when he was accused of killing a cat

During his four years at Inter Milan, Luis Figo won four Serie A titles – but he was also accused of intentionally running over a black cat at their training ground so, yer know, there was good and bad.

Figo’s first goal for Inter was not a memorable one. In fact, so low were the stakes during the ‘Sky TV Trophy’ in August 2005, only around 300 spectators saw Inter win 2-1 against Al-Ittihad in what was essentially a 60-minute kickabout.

No video evidence exists of Figo’s goal in the fourth minute, but the match report on Inter’s website tells us it was “spettacolare”. Given what we know about Figo, that’s not hard to believe.

Former Inter enigma Mohamed Kallon later scored a consolation for the Saudi club.

From that point on, things would get a little more serious for Figo. At the age of 32, the Portugal legend was looking for one final challenge that would do justice to his already spectacular career.

Inter seemed a sensible choice. They were a club going places. The season before, they had won the Coppa Italia and finished third in Serie A, losing just twice all season.

A 22-year-old Adriano had scored 28 goals in all competitions, and other key members of the squad included Francesco Toldo, Javier Zanetti, Ivan Cordoba, Esteban Cambiasso and Dejan Stankovic.

It was a strong side but one in which the right-wing berth was very much up for grabs: the year before, it had been occupied in shifts by Andy Van der Meyde and Brazilian wingback Ze Maria.

That made Figo something of an automatic pick for his debut season. But few fans at the San Siro expected the midfielder to acclimatise quite so quickly and comfortably.

Figo began the 2005–06 campaign playing on the wing or behind two strikers in a midfield diamond, often moving around to confuse opponents (and Inter staff).

He scored his first real goal for Inter on November 20 against Parma, latching onto a Juan Sebastian Veron through ball and dinking past the keeper.

A few weeks later the winger, now 33, claimed a hat-trick of assists in a 4-0 rout of Reggina.

The new signing was enjoying himself, playing with a level of freedom that was apparently all of his own making.

“I don’t tell him to stay on the wing or move him if he moves to the middle,” explained manager Roberto Mancini. “Figo knows he can go and play where he wants at a certain point in the match if he feels it’s right.”

Inter’s midfield had improved, but the team didn’t see an immediate uptick in results.

Although Inter eventually won more matches than they had in 2004–05, they increased their number of defeats by six, and by the end of the campaign their 76 points were only enough for another third-place finish.

As it turned out, the Calciopoli scandal of 2006 saw Juventus and Milan retroactively docked points, launching Inter into first place and earning them their first Serie A title since 1989.

It was a lucky turn of events for Inter and Figo, though they would need little luck over the next few seasons.

Ahead of the 2006–07 campaign, Inter signed Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Patrick Vieira from relegated Juventus and were boosted by handicaps to their nearest rivals.

Juventus were left to fight for their future in Serie B, while strong sides like AC Milan and Fiorentina were docked points, effectively neutering their title aspirations before the season began.

On an individual level, things got off to the brightest possible start for Figo.

In the Supercoppa Italiana, the first game of the domestic season, Inter fought back from 3-0 down to beat Roma 4-3 in extra time, with Figo hitting the winning goal in the 94th minute — his finest strike in black and blue.

With an even stronger team and weakened rivals, Inter cruised to a second consecutive title, breaking records along the way. Between October 2006 and late February 2007, the club won 17 consecutive league matches.

But the 34-year-old Figo found himself in and out of the side, and over this period his relationship with Mancini became strained.

The midfielder later said: “I have always behaved in the same professional way, but [Mancini] showed a lack of respect with some of his choices. A coach is always free to criticise his players, but Mancini did it in the wrong way with me.”

And so, after just one and a half seasons, the Portuguese agreed a transfer away from Inter — to an unlikely destination.

In January 2007, it was announced that Al-Ittihad, the team against whom Figo scored his first Inter ‘goal’ in front of a handful of fans, would be the midfielder’s next club.

The Saudi team had made a generous offer, described modestly by their chairman as “one of the biggest contracts ever seen in the Middle East”.

“I was looking for a soft solution,” he said. “I didn’t want to retire immediately. This way I can play another five or six months of light soccer.”

He added that he “needed to feel important”, suggesting that Mancini’s squad rotation was not to his liking.

As Inter played out the second half of the 2006–07 season at walking pace, eventually winning the Serie A title with five games to spare, there were disagreements happening behind the scenes between Figo and Al-Ittihad.

In May, after scoring his only two league goals of the season in the final two games, Figo called off the Saudi deal, citing breach of contract.

The collapse of the move left Figo in limbo, but Inter president Massimo Moratti ultimately convinced the midfielder to sign a new one-year deal — with the promise that he could become an international ambassador for the club at the end of the season.

Despite tensions with Mancini, Figo stayed on.

Over the 2007–08 campaign, a 35-year-old Figo was in and out of the side, and his playing time was limited further when he broke his fibula after just 11 games.

When he returned to action in February, Inter were top of the table, but the veteran midfielder was mostly limited to cameos from the bench.

Then, towards the end of the season, strange things started happening.

During the second week of May 2008, a journalist named Vittorio Feltri, editor of the newspaper Libero, accused Figo of intentionally killing a black cat.

The cat “loved to stretch out on the grass where the Inter players would practice”, wrote Feltri, who accused a superstitious Figo of running over the animal to alleviate bad luck.

“It is completely untrue,” Figo responded. “I want [Libero] to apologise otherwise I will be obliged to take legal action.”

Protestors reportedly waited for Figo at Inter’s training ground, holding banners displaying messages like, ‘Figo, you’ve killed a black cat, the whole world is disgusted with you.’

As it was, most Inter fans were actually pretty happy with Figo. Not because of the cat business but because of the player’s professionalism and largely excellent performances over three seasons in Italy.

Another person definitely not disgusted with Figo was president Moratti, the man in charge. And it was Moratti’s loyalty to the midfielder that may have ultimately led to another significant event that month.

Despite Inter’s Serie A success, the club sacked Mancini at the end of May — officially because of comments made by the manager about leaving the club; unofficially because of his perceived cruelty to Figo, the more popular of the two men.

With Figo due to begin his ambassadorial work with Inter that summer, the sacking of Mancini gave him food for thought.

But when Jose Mourinho was announced as the new Inter manager, the club did not find it difficult to coax their skilful veteran into a fourth and final season.

Figo actually played more in 2008–09 than he had during Mancini’s final campaign. And though mostly used from the bench, he enjoyed his new role under Mourinho, helping the club to its fourth consecutive league title and laying the foundations for bigger glories still to come.

He scored his final goal for the club, a leaping header, in February 2009 during a 3-0 win against Lecce, and on his last ever appearance he was given the captain’s armband by Javier Zanetti.

Few players could command such respect over such a short period.

Figo’s perfect record of four Serie A medals in four years — his last won at the age of 37 — are a testament to his ability and dedication right up to the end.

What’s shocking is that, had Al-Ittihad got their way and signed Figo in January 2007, he might have left Italy with just one.

Maybe the collapse of that move was a stroke of luck. But it wasn’t one gained by sinister means: in 2012, Vittorio Feltri admitted that the black cat story was nonsense.

#1438. Bayern star creeping up on sublime Barcelona duo in WhoScored rankings for 2026-27

Who are the best-performing players across Europe’s top five leagues this season? We’ve turned to their WhoScored ratings to find out.

WhoScored‘s comprehensive system of player ratings is based on a whole host of stats, which give an indication of who’s playing well and who’s not.

As the season progresses, we’ll be keeping track of the top 10 highest-rated players in Europe’s top five leagues. Right now, there’s no one from the Premier League…

Bellingham had a brightish start to the season with Real Madrid and got himself back among the scorers at the weekend against Racing Santander in his highest-rated performance of the season so far.

Sinayoko’s numbers have swelled in recent weeks. Of his eight goals and five assists this season for Paris FC, four each have come in his last three games.

Unsurprisingly, he’s been the highest-rated player in two of them.

Stuttgart lost their last two matches before the break, but Mittelstadt received a man-of-the-match rating in both of them. It wouldn’t be a massive shock to see the 29-year-old Germany international move on in the summer if the Swabians regress to the mean and fail to qualify for Europe again.

It’s been a decent start to the season for Werder Bremen and Austrian midfielder Grull has stood out.

He both scored and assisted, with a man-of-the-match rating, as they defeated RB Leipzig and Augsburg at the Weser Stadium. Grull even came out of their opening weekend 4-1 tonking at Freiburg with credit, earning an 8.01 match rating in the heavy loss.

He was the highest-rated player against Borussia Dortmund when they got back from the international break and has made an assist in each of his last two game.s

Quite simply incredible last season and seeing little reason to change that, Kane has four goals and six assists so far in the Bundesliga this season.

Since the international break, he’s been more about the assists (five) than the goals (one) in the league, but it just shows he really can do it all.

RB Leipzig prospect Nusa has four goals and six assists to his name so far this season. We’re pretty sure the big clubs will be circling.

He was the match winner on Halloween against Schalke with a goal and assist in a 2-0 win.

Still only 21, the winger has a big future ahead of him.

Mbappe came second for the Ballon d’Or this year, but mission 2027 is well underway.

A hat-trick against Real Sociedad in Madrid’s second game of the season showed Mbappe means business after a summer in which he became the World Cup’s leading scorer of all time.

The French forward has also scored braces against Rayo Vallecano, Sevilla and Barcelona, helping him creep up on the leaders here.

By last season’s standards, Olise had a bit of a quiet start to 2026-27. Just one goal and zero assists in their first three Bundesliga outings of the campaign, which included a goalless draw at newly-promoted Schalke and a narrow 2-1 victory over minnows Elversberg.

But his 10.0 masterclass in the Champions League against Bodo/Glimt (two goals and an assist) hinted that last term was no flash in the pan. He remains one of Europe’s most devastating, elite forwards. A hat-trick and another 10.0 rating in a 7-0 mauling of Union Berlin catapulted him into the top five, and a goal-and-assist performance against RB Leipzig lifted him higher into the top three.

Back in January, we declared Raphinha the best player in the world, asking the question:

“Is there another player in world football who can claim to elevate their team as much as Raphinha? In a collective sport, isn’t that the most important thing?”

That take didn’t age all that well, as the Brazilian suffered a frustratingly injury-ravaged latter half of the 2025-26 campaign and struggled to make an impact at the World Cup as a result.

But look at him now. After being converted into a striker, Raphinha has been on fire this season. Fifteen(!) goals and three assists in La Liga so far, averaging a goal contribution every 40 minutes.

Even when he failed to find the net for the first time this season, Raphinha set up two goals in Barca’s 4-2 win over Levante. And then returned with back-to-back hat-tricks. He is the top scorer across Europe.

Quite simply, Yamal is taking his game to new levels this season. Ten goals and seven assists in La Liga from just 11 games. El Clasico was the first time since August he’d played in a Barcelona game without contributing to a goal.

Barca’s failure to win that game knocked his rating down a bit here, but he’s still top of the tree.

And yep, he’s still only 19. This lad is ridiculous. He has completed the most dribbles across Europe.

#1437. Comparing Harry Kane’s incredible stats since the start of 2025-26 with Kylian Mbappe’s

Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d’Or in 2026 – deservedly, we reckon – and they’ll both be looking to keep up their world-class standards this season.

Kane scored more goals than anyone else across Europe’s major leagues last season, but Mbappe was the top scorer in the Champions League and the 2026 World Cup.

Kane and Mbappe faced off in last season’s Champions League quarter-finals between Bayern Munich and Real Madrid, as well as the World Cup third-place play-off between England and France.

Across their whole careers for club and country, they have a combined 998 goals.

And though neither of them have ever won the Champions League still, they are rightly regarded as two of the best players in the world.

Here’s how the two players have compared since the start of last season for their clubs.

Kane is a player we’ve become accustomed to seeing score more than 30 or 40 goals in a season, stretching back to his time with Tottenham.

But the 2025-26 campaign was the highest-scoring in his career with 61 goals, better than the 44 he got in his first season with Bayern.

He also surpassed his best-ever goalscoring campaign in the Champions League after scoring 11 in Europe last season.

Braces against Chelsea, Pafos and Union SG in the league phase helped his tally, as did a double in the second leg of their last-16 win over Atalanta.

Kane enjoyed two eight-game scoring streaks in all competitions last season and bagged hat tricks against RB Leipzig, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

He reached double figures of goals for the new season after 11 games.

After surpassing the 40-goal mark in both his last season with PSG and first with Real Madrid, Mbappe reached the same milestone again last season.

He will no doubt have harboured some frustrations at seeing his former teammates win the Champions League last season while Madrid made only the quarter-finals.

However, he has been on a mission since. Last season was his highest-scoring Champions League campaign; he has now overtaken Raul’s tally to enter the all-time top five competition goalscorers.

Braces against Marseille, Monaco and Benfica, a hat trick against Kairat and four goals against Olympiacos were the fruits of his efforts in last season’s league phase, before his goals in each leg against Bayern.

But Madrid’s elimination in the quarter-finals again means Mbappe will have to wait until the end of this season at least to stand a chance of finally winning the competition.

He’s started with a goal per game in it this season.

#1436. 12 forgotten ballers now playing in the Qatar Stars League: Mitrovic, Verratti…

Footballers moving to the Middle East has become part and parcel of the modern game, but it’s usually the ones going to Saudi Arabia you hear more about.

Qatar, after hosting the 2022 World Cup, isn’t sitting back when it comes to investing in some big footballing names either.

Familiar names like Roberto Firmino and Riyad Mahrez have ended up there, along with a fair few players you probably haven’t thought about for longer. Like these.

Serie A enthusiasts will remember a time when Piatek was all the rage. For a couple of months, at least.

Talk about a good first impression. A four-goal haul on his debut in the Coppa Italia before scoring nine goals in his first seven Serie A games for Genoa. Wowsers.

A mid-season step up to AC Milan followed and Piatek made a reasonable start there too, before taking the cursed number nine shirt for his second season and never quite being the same.

Piatek went on to play for Hertha Berlin, Fiorentina and Salernitana before finding his shooting boots again during a two-year stint with Istanbul Basaksehir.

He moved from there to Al Duhail in 2025, scoring nine league goals in his first season in Qatar.

A World Cup winner with Germany in 2014, Draxler went on to become a four-time Ligue 1 winner with PSG, plus a Primeira Liga winner with Benfica.

He left Europe behind in 2023 to move to Al Ahli SC, a club based in Doha (not to be confused with the Saudi Pro League side where Ivan Toney plays).

The attacking midfielder scored six goals from 11 games in his first season in Qatar before 12 from 18 in his second and seven from 20 in his third.

It’s been a decent start to the season for the 33-year-old this time too, with three goals from eight games so far.

A new entrant into the Qatar Stars League this summer, Bennacer joined Al-Gharafa from AC Milan.

The one-time Arsenal man had spent the last 18 months of his time with Milan out on loan, first at Marseille and then at Dinamo Zagreb, before his contract got terminated.

A month later, he signed for Al-Gharafa on a two-year deal. But he got sent off on his debut for the club in the Asian Champions League against Saudi side Al Hilal.

A move from Saudi Arabia to Qatar has become fairly common for ageing players who were once shiny new toys in the Saudi Pro League but become surplus to requirements.

It happened to Firmino, it happened to Mahrez and it happened to Brozovic too.

Best known for his eight-year spell with Inter and as part of the Croatia sides that excelled in the 2018 and 2022 World Cups, Brozovic spent three years with Al-Nassr before a September switch to Al Sadd.

The midfielder was only able to make one appearance for his new club before being sidelined with a groin injury.

A popular player in his time at Porto, Brahimi has been playing in Qatar since he left the Portuguese giants in 2019.

The winger first spent three years with Al-Rayyan before joining current employers Al-Gharafa in 2022.

He’s captained them in most of their games this season, scoring five goals from eight games in the league.

Widely considered the best Italian player to never play in Serie A, Verratti spent his peak years winning trophies galore in France with PSG – a club, of course, with Qatari owners.

When he reached the end of his time in Paris, he was conveniently sold to Al-Arabi for €45m.

Two years later, the midfielder made a move across Doha to join rivals Al Duhail, where he still plays now.

Joselu had his moment in the sun back with Real Madrid in the 2023-24 season, but that was all he got there.

He was swiftly sold to Al-Gharafa for a two-year stint there, before embarking on a new challenge in the same league in October with a free transfer to Al-Sailiya.

The former Stoke and Newcastle striker scored on just his second appearance for his new club.

The less said about his season in the Premier League with Aston Villa the better, but Veretout went on to have a decent career in Serie A and Ligue 1, playing for clubs like Fiorentina, Roma and Marseille.

In 2025, the midfielder left Lyon for Al-Arabi, where he scored twice from 22 Qatar Stars League appearances in his debut season.

He has one goal to his name this season – the last covered by his contract as things stand – as well.

His Liverpool days are very much forgotten but Alberto was a more than decent baller for Lazio.

After eight years in Serie A, he left them in 2024 to join Al Duhail, before making a cross-Qatari transfer two years later to Al-Wakrah.

Former Leeds striker Rodrigo is now onto his third Qatari club. First he joined Al-Rayyan in 2023, before having a loan spell with Al-Gharafa in 2024-25.

This summer he signed for Lusail, newly promoted to the Qatar Stars League.

He’s done well so far with five goals from his first eight league games with the club.

Sarabia arrived at Wolves in 2023 with a decent-looking CV, including spells with Sevilla and PSG after coming through the Real Madrid ranks.

The midfielder left Wolves when his contract expired in 2025 and signed for Al-Arabi.

He enjoyed a decent debut season in Qatar with nine league goals from 21 games.

It was a bit of a shame to see Mitrovic leave the Premier League for Saudi Arabia in 2023. He’d done pretty well for Fulham and probably still had something to give at a good level.

But after his two years with Al Hilal came to an end, he didn’t head back to Europe. Instead, he stuck in the Middle East with Al Rayyan.

He scored five goals from 11 games in an injury-hit debut season in the Qatar Stars League.

#1435. Top-scoring attacking trios in 2026-27: Barcelona way out in front already

Bayern Munich had the best front three in Europe last season, but there’s already a different runaway leader this time around.

We’ve taken a closer look at the highest-scoring trios across the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 this season. It doesn’t matter whether the three players were on the pitch at the same time or not, just how many goals each team’s three best scorers have got.

It’s very much the early days of this ranking, so expect plenty of change as the season wears on.

But for now, here are the top 10 attacking trios in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

Barcelona have banished any fears they’d have a void up front after the Pole’s exit this summer, with Raphinha reborn as a centre-forward. And a pretty good one at that, too.

Lamine Yamal is in his typically outrageous form as well, and so Barca are way out in front with their best three-way combination for goals this season.

We imagine five-goal Fermin Lopez might not be part of the trio for much longer, since he isn’t really playing as an attacker anyway. Anthony Gordon, your time will come.

Jose Mourinho’s second Real Madrid reign hasn’t been the most convincing so far, but it’s helped that some of his star attackers are still doing the business.

That’s especially the case with Kylian Mbappe, who’s scored 12 goals in La Liga so far – including a brace in El Clasico.

Jude Bellingham has chipped in with a few as well and summer signing Yan Diomande has netted three times.

Highlights have included a 3-0 win at Fiorentina, beating Cesc Fabregas’ Como and knocking four past Sassuolo and five past Lecce.

Antonio Raimondo leads the way with eight, with midfielder Giacomo Calo adding five and winger Giorgi Kvernadze contributing three. Consider them firmly on our radar.

Raimondo will be out for a few months though with an injury, just as he was starting to flourish. Football can be cruel.

Esteban Lepaul is the star here, with seven goals already after netting 20 last season. No wonder he recently made his international debut for France.

Boulaye Dia and Sebastien Szymanski have chipped in with four each too.

Never mind the off-field distractions, it’s been business as usual on the pitch for City.

Erling Haaland has gone nine from nine so far in the Premier League and Rayan Cherki has already matched his total of four from last season.

No one quite knows what these goals are going towards, but until a recent slip-up or two, City are by and large just beating what’s in front of them for now.

Last year’s most prolific trio are really starting to kick up a gear, scoring five goals between them in Bayern’s 6-1 win over RB Leipzig.

Michael Olise currently leads the way with six, but Luis Diaz was the hat-trick scorer against Leipzig and Kane will hit double figures before your next bedtime.

Roma have been enjoying their highest-scoring 10-game run at the start of a season in Serie A with 28 goals.

Half of those have come from Donyell Malen, Rodrigo Mora and Matias Soule, which has become their best option for a front three while Paulo Dybala has been injured.

It’s Malen doing most of the heavy lifting with eight goals in the league so far.

Hang on a minute. Yep, that’s Niclas Fullkrug, the worst Premier League signing of all time.

He’s a man reborn at Werder Bremen this season with nine goals. Shoutout to Marco Grull as well, who’s assisted four of them (and three for other teammates) as well as scoring twice himself.

JP Morgan? CPR? We’ve seen some frankly awful shouts for what Chelsea’s new front three should go by, but one thing’s for sure – they seem to have clicked straight away.

Morgan Rogers was the missing ingredient, joining Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer in a big-money (OK, huge money) move from Aston Villa in the summer.

He’s hit the ground running with five goals in the league so far, the same amount as striker Pedro.

An attacking trio featuring a midfielder, a 20-year-old and a wing-back. Fair enough.

Milan will be hoping big summer signing Goncalo Ramos can start repaying their faith, but for now, their main scorers have been Adrien Rabiot, Alphadjo Cisse and Diego Moreira.

#1434. Highest scoring centre-backs in Premier League history: Gabriel, Terry, Kompany…

Gabriel Magalhaes has chipped in with several goals for Arsenal, but where does he rank among the highest-scoring centre-backs in Premier League history?

The Brazilian has made a name for himself as a goalscoring defender and has become particularly lethal from set-piece situations.

Given how dangerous Arsenal have become in that department, it’s no surprise that the 28-year-old has scored so many goals over the past six years.

In fact, since making his debut for Arsenal in 2020-21, he’s scored more goals (21), than any other Premier League defender.

The likes of Fabian Schar, Virgil van Dijk, Michael Keane, Kurt Zouma, John Stones, Ben Mee and Lewis Dunk have also scored double figures in that time, but none have scored more than Gabriel.

“That shows a lot and not only set-pieces strategy but also mentality,” Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino told BBC MOTD when describing Gabriel’s goal against Newcastle back in September 2025.

“Other teams if they get six/seven corners and they don’t score, they start to lose belief in the qualities but for us it’s a matter of keep doing what we do, doing it at the highest level and in the end the last one, last second, we scored and I’m really happy.”

In the wider context of the all-time standings, the Brazilian defender is now joint 10th.

He’s now only one goal away from matching Laurent Koscielny’s Premier League tally and is only four goals away from securing a place in the top five.

Unsurprisingly, John Terry tops the list with a mammoth 41 league goals. Second on the list is Ian Marshall with 33 goals, although he did spend a portion of his career playing as a forward.

The rest of the top five is then made up of Virgil van Dijk, Gary Cahill and William Gallas.

Providing that Gabriel remains in the Premier League for the foreseeable future, there’s a chance that he could retire as the second-highest-scoring centre-back in the league’s history.

Admittedly, catching up to Terry’s record of 41 goals does seem out of reach, even for Gabriel.

Michael Keane – 19 goals =14. Ugo Ehiogu – 19 goals =16. Fabian Schar – 18 goals =16. Nathan Ake – 18 goals =16. Vincent Kompany – 18 goals =16. Phil Jagielka – 18 goals =19.
