G.d.J., F.M., T.G., O.L., R.M., S.B., O.S. and O.A.B. conceived of the study. R.M. provided GB tissue samples, aided by T.S., A.Y. and H.B. F.M. led experimental design, histology, Visium ST data generation and tissue processing for multi-omic profiling. E.T., S.R., I. Mulas and M. Patel contributed to histology and Visium ST data generation. T.G. coordinated multi-omic profiling, led single-nuclei multiome data generation, sample logistics and management. G.S. performed GBO experiments with contributions from T.G., F.M. and H.B. S. Eckert, D.Z., A.O., H.P., K.K., I. Mamun, Z.K. and E.P. contributed to single-nuclei multiome data generation. O.G. led sequence library generation for multiome and Visium ST data, aided by Y.W., S. Eckert and T.P. M.D. generated LCM-WGS data. K. Roberts and A.L.T. generated Xenium data from patient tumours. C.T., H.M.C., H.J., B.R., H.A., J.H. and V.B.P. generated Xenium data from GBOs. J.D.B.-S. generated immunohistochemistry data. G.d.J. led multiome, ST and LCM-WGS data processing and analysis, and interpreted results. M.J. performed histopathological annotations of Visium ST data, validated by A.Q. and M.B. O.L. developed the SpaceTree model, applied the model to Visium ST data and interpreted results. A.A., S. Er and Y.C. performed cell2fate trajectory analysis and interpreted results. Q.Z. and A.S.R. contributed to myeloid cell state annotation and CCC analysis. Z.S. and M.G. contributed to Xenium panel design. H.M. and K.R. analysed patient Xenium data. K.R., P.M., S.M. and L.J. performed ST deconvolution benchmarks. J.T.H.L. and S.M. assisted with ST data processing. R.P. developed the GBM-space data portal for multi-omic data with contributions from J.C. and M. Prete. O.G. coordinated raw data submission to data repositories. L.R.-G., M.S. and M.M. contributed to interpretation of GBM cell states. J.S.-R. supervised CCC analysis. J.B. supervised histopathological annotation and immunohistochemistry validation. D.H.R. supervised myeloid data interpretation. S.B. supervised LCM-WGS data generation, analysis and interpretation. O.S. supervised SpaceTree model development, application and data interpretation. O.A.B. supervised cell atlassing data generation, analysis and interpretation. G.d.J., F.M. and O.A.B. prepared figures. G.d.J. and O.A.B. wrote the paper with feedback from all authors.

a) Overview of grid-like sampling strategy for tumour AT15. b) Distributions of common RNA QC metrics (number of genes by counts, total counts, mitochondrial read fraction, and doublet scores) post-filtering across major coarse-grained cell states. Boxplots display median, IQR, and 1.5x IQR whiskers for n = 1,025,329 nuclei summarised across n = 155 10X reactions. c) Summary of ATAC QC metrics and applied QC filters. From left to right: nuclei passing generic ArchR filters, nuclei passing both generic ArchR filters and RNA filters, and promoter ratio compared against minimum fragments.Generic ArchR filters indicated by solid lines (minimum unique fragments ≥ 1000 and TSS enrichments ≥ 4). Dashed lines represent target minimum values for the respective metrics.

a) Visium ST sections from each sampling site of tumour AT10 coloured according to GB cell state abundances derived from cell2location mapping. The top seven most frequently observed states at the tumour-level were visualised, with colour intensity proportional to inferred cell state abundance. Broader trends, particularly areas of cell state co-localisation are highlighted in bold text. b) Images depict overlayed cell2location-derived cell state abundances (colour intensity) for the highest-abundance cell states (colour) across each tumour. The top 7 cell states were selected on the basis of ranked maximum abundance. One section from a single site was included (top left).

a) Tissue microenvironment summaries. Left: Most frequently observed cell state (column) found within each microenvironment (row). Dotplot shows the proportion of the top cell state per spatial microenvironment averaged across tumours (size) and the average Pearson’s correlation coefficient (r) across tumours. Centre: Relative frequency of each microenvironment across tumours (size and colour). Right: Correlation of spatial microenvironments with histopathological features annotated on Visium H&E images based on IvyGAP annotations (columns). Dotplot shows the proportion of spots associated with a spatial microenvironment which overlap with a given histological feature (size) and the point biserial correlation coefficient (r) between feature annotations and spatial microenvironment abundance. b) Tissue microenvironment (colour) abundance (colour intensity) overlaid on Visium H&Es for a subset of patients, demonstrating microenvironment regionalisation. Microenvironments with the highest max abundance were visualised.

a) Dotplot depicting common EMT markers compared to markers associated with astrogliosis. Colour intensity is the mean expression across a cell state with min-max normalisation applied across each gene. Dot size corresponds to the proportion of cells in a group expressing a given gene (expression greater than 0). Colours correspond to groups of EMT-associated genes and genes associated with both EMT and astrogliosis (including “Astrogliosis pathways”). b) Immunofluorescent staining of GB tissue section revealing distinct patterns of AKAP12 (AC-gliosis) and HILPDA (hypoxic) protein expression. Panels show single channels of a region of interest (scale bar: 100 µm). Imaging performed for n = 3 tumours, independently. c) Xenium section demonstrating zonation of AC-gliosis-hypoxia cell states ranging from infiltrated grey matter to the necrotic tumour core.

a) LCM-informed CNA calling workflow to predict snRNA-seq CN events via alleleIntegrator. The scatterplot (top right) represents the B-allele frequency (BAF) for sample PD60966a_lo0005. Colours correspond to SNP allele frequency of the major (red) and minor (blue) alleles. The UMAP (bottom right) shows alleleIntegrator clone calls superimposed on the visualisation such that cells with chr17 CNs (light blue) can be distinguished from cells without chr17 CNs (orange). b) Barplots depicting cell state distributions across clones (right) and clone distribution across tumour sampling sites (left) in LCM-WGS informed clones. c) Sankey plot depicting concordant clone assignment across multiome and LCM-informed CNA calling methods per cell. d) Phylogeny of SNV clusters across AT3 LCM-WGS samples. Branch length corresponds to mutation counts on a natural logarithmic scale. Clusters are coloured according to their cluster IDs in Fig. 4e. Mutation counts associated with each SNV cluster are indicated in square brackets. e) Analysis of clonal intermixture using Rao’s quadratic entropy (Rao’s Q). Rao’s Q is displayed for each LCM ROI (columns). Tree-bound SNV cluster frequencies (right) are also depicted, showing the relative distribution of SNV clusters nested in a phylogenetic context. f) LCM-WGS- and SpaceTree-based spatial clone mapping workflows. g) Spatial clonal domains compared across LCM-WGS pyclone deconvolution and Visium ST SpaceTree mapping across matching tissue locations. Domains were defined by Bray-Curtis clustering of clone distributions within each ROI across each modality. H&E images depict tissue locations used for LCM colored by SpaceTree clone clusters (left) and pyclone-VI clone clusters (right). The sankey plot demonstrates ROI cluster assignment between modalities. h) SpaceTree distinguishes tumour versus normal regions and resolves spatial clonal domains in tumours. Top: Visium section from tumour AT15 showing SpaceTree mapping of diploid versus malignant subclones to infiltrated and bulk tumour regions, respectively. Bottom: Spatial clonal domains identified by clustering SpaceTree-derived clonal composition of Visium spots. i) SpaceTree cell state (left) and clonal (centre and right) maps of tumour AT10 resolves distinct regional distributions of the chr17-CNA subclone. j) Tumour purity of infiltrated versus tumour tissue microenvironments estimated by SpaceTree, summarised at the Visium spot level (n = 97 Visium sections). Boxplots display median, IQR, and 1.5x IQR whiskers.

a) Cellular trajectory analysis workflow. b) Scatterplot depicting major QC metrics for cell2fate trajectory results. Patches correspond to QC thresholds: maximum latent time > 25 (red), and average transition score > 0.2 (yellow). Trajectories below the maximum latent time threshold (grey) were omitted from analysis, and those passing were used (blue) but flagged if they fell beneath the transition score threshold. c) Clones which passed trajectory QC thresholds (blue) compared to those which were omitted (grey) for each tumour. d) Boxplot summarising min-max normalised latent time for each cell state across all clones passing QC thresholds (A). Box colour corresponds to cell class. Boxplots display median, IQR, and 1.5x IQR whiskers (n = 88,495 cells across n = 11 high-diversity clones). e) Boxplot summarising transition scores between granular cell states in among clones passing cell2fate QC threshold (Extended Data Fig. 6b). Transitions (x-axis) are denoted by “>” and are ordered such that the first cell state transitions into the second. Colours (shared with Extended Data Fig. 6d) correspond to the cell classes involved in the transition. Boxplots colours are split by source (left) and target (right) cell classes. The red dashed line represents the threshold for transition scores used during QC. Boxplots show median, IQR, and 1.5x IQR whiskers (n = 559 total observed cell state transitions across a total of 23 clones).

a) Histograms showing cell class distribution across latent time for each clone passing QC thresholds. Colours correspond to cell class. The x-axis represents min-max normalised latent time.

a) Recurrent temporal gene expression modules are conserved across the trajectories of 23 tumour subclones. Heatmap (left) displays top marker gene overlap (n = 200) across factors associated with each meta-module. Colour bars correspond to marker overlap proportion and average latent time across each recurrent module. Additional heatmap (right) depicts the cell2fate meta-module enrichment among coarse-grained states. Colour corresponds to z-score normalised mean relative expression scores for each cell state. Rows are shared between heatmaps and ordered by average min-max normalised latent time observed across each meta-module. b) Spatial mapping of key temporal modules (colours) from subclone AT15_4 onto its matching Visium section (right). Network diagram (bottom) shows the mean pairwise euclidean distance between temporal modules for the associated Visium section. c) Activation patterns of genes (top) and meta-modules (bottom) for clone AT15_3 summarising the inferred cellular trajectory. Cell2fate derived activation plots of temporal gene expression modules (top) and top marker genes of each module (bottom) with matched colours. d) Example of TF expression rate over time for TFs implicated in three different stages of inferred latent time across three clones (AT9_2, AT15_3, and AT4_1): early time (top), mid-range time (middle), and late time (bottom) TFs. Line plots are summarising TF rate across all stated clones. Colours correspond to TF identity.

a) GFP epifluorescence images of D7 GBOs infiltrated by E25 and E30 GB cell lines (left) and close up images of infiltrating single cells (right). Right, top panel: Epifluorescence image showing GBO infiltration at D7. Right, bottom panel: GFP transcripts (green spots) marking engrafted cells overlaid on Xenium images showing DAPI (blue) and cell segmentation panel (pink-yellow-green). Scale bars: 500 µm (top), 20 µm (bottom). Imaging performed for n = 3 independent GBOs. b) UMAPs summarising scVI integration of our cell atlas with GBO data (left) and scANVI label transfer results using our coarse-grained cell state annotation (right). c) Dotplots showing expression of GB cell state marker genes in our Xenium data for cell state identifies transferred using scANVI. Dot size corresponds to the proportion of cells expressing a gene within a given group, dot colour corresponds to normalised expression within a given group (see legend at bottom of panel). Plots show GBO and engrafted cells pooled across all timepoints. d) Spatial plots showing zonated cell state organisation of GBOs using label-transferred cell state identities (top) and marker gene expression (bottom). Marker gene expression colour intensity maps to log1p normalised gene expression as indicated by colourbars. e) Line plot summarising cell state proportions of GFP+ engrafted cells across E25 (top) and E30 (bottom) organoids for each time point. Points correspond to proportions from individual organoids. Colour corresponds to the data modalities, where pre-engrafted scRNA-seq are indicated in orange, and GFP+ cells mapped via Xenium are indicated in blue.

a) Myeloid heterogeneity in our multimodal atlas. Dendrogram depicts transcriptomic clustering of myeloid subcluster snRNA-seq profiles annotated to three major phenotypic classes (background colors). Stacked bar plots depict the relative distribution of myeloid states across tumours and the proportion of top myeloid activity signatures from Miller at al. per state. Dotplots show key marker gene expression and selected term enrichment across states. The spatial correlation dotplot depicts the enrichment of myeloid cell states in cell2location TMs (prop) and the Pearson correlation coefficient between cell state abundances and TM niche abundance (r). b) Spatial co-localisation of distinct malignant and myeloid states. Visium sections (left) show cell2location abundances of top cell states in tumour AT15 with colours mapping to corresponding labels highlighted in the boxes to the right. Malignant cell states are grouped according to their trajectory and myeloid cell states are grouped according to their phenotypic classes and their spatial organisation. c) Schematic detailing the spatially resolved cell-cell communication analysis strategy to detect signalling from distinct myeloid subtypes to their spatially co-localised malignant states that recur across multiple tumours. d) Myeloid ligands predicted to signal to distinct malignant cell states by spatially-resolved cell-cell communication analysis. Genes correspond to top ligands identified in myeloid signalling factors identified by tensor decomposition analysis. Dotplot represents the proportion of myeloid cells expressing the ligand (size) and relative expression across cell states (colour). e) Overview of major cell-cell interactions identified between regional myeloid (sender) and distinct malignant (receiver) cell states.

#1361. Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel said when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

I thought we were very professional second half. We stepped up and needed to be more dynamic, bring more urgency into our play, which we did. We kept that intensity going and and the effort was till there. Deserved victory.

Strange to get an early red card. Not the best for the spectators, not the best for the team. It’s an awkward one. But we got the win.

To guide it into the goal, there was an awful lot [for Anthony Gordon] to do. Good pass, good goal. Both full-backs were good. The position in the second half suited Trent more than the position in the first half. Lewis was excellent on the other side.

We have used all the outfield players after two matches so credit to all of them. Now it’s important to relax and enjoy the evening, do a good recovery and prepare for Saturday.

I think it was good. They go down to 10 men and it should be easier for us to win the game, But in fact it makes it more difficult. They get very compact and defend with a lot of players around the box and it’s hard to break them down.

We got that [goal] at the start of the second half which is what we needed. The longer it’s 0-0, it gets harder and harder and harder.

[Where do you place your assist?]  It’s up there for sure. I spoke to Ant at half-time and said if I get into those half-spaces I’m looking to put it in so make sure you get to the back post. I didn’t expect it to work so quickly.

He’s a willing runner, great to play with him. I saw the run and was able to execute the pass,

It’s always a pleasure and an honour to represent my country. It’s been a long time. I’ve always believed that I can play for England and I want to. The manager’s given me the opportunity and I tried to do what he wanted me to do to the best of my ability and I hope he’s happy with how I played.

🦁 #1301Alex Scott reflects on a special night, earning his first senior England cap 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/lC34bAPbbd

It was good, quite dominant. We created a lot of chances but without the quality. When they went a man down, we were too passive at times. We need to be dominant, as I said earlier, go for the throat and put teams away.

I’ve missed playing with Hally. He’s a good lad. We had great chemistry at Newcastle and it’s great to share this stage with him.

It’s my only header. I’d be the worst header of the ball you’ll ever see. Really happy, resally proud to score that because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.

Perfectly competent and signs of promise in the left-back/left-wing axis. England looked too open against 11 men and better teams – hola España – may have capitalised on the sloppiness. But once Sulc was sent off, England gradually turned the screw and created a hatful of chances, running out easy winners.

Another tidy save from Kovar when Bellingham receives a pass from the left, strides towards the D, then drives a daisy-cutter towards the left of goal. The keeper swoops down early to turn it behind with a stiff wrist.

Two minutes of stoppage time are signalled as England try to pen the home side in their own half.

Tuchel has kept the back four on the pitch for the 90 minutes. He was not entirely happy with them in the first half – or his body language suggested that, anyway. But it is a welcomed clean sheet for England after the chaotic defeats to Spain and France.

Ngumoha is enjoying himself and showing off some excellent close control.

Scott and Eze smash shots over the bar from 22 yards within a minute of each other.

Rogers’ diagonal cross is chested down by Eze as he sets up an opportunity to shoot in the area but a defender hacks it away. Ngumoha pounces on the loose ball and plays a neat reverse pass with the outside of his boot to Rogers on the underlap. Rogers goes for power rather than lift to find Eze or Bellingham and the keeper makes another smart save.

Gibbs-White’s pace and direct running have the beating of Chaloupek and he tees up Eze to hammer a left-foot shot that seemed to be arrowing into the net until Kovar stuck up his right hand to paw it over.

Gordon stops, then from a standing start drives past bursts past Chaloupek to the byline and stands up a near-post cross that Rogers flashes wide.

Czech Republic break after England’s attack down the right hits the skids. Hlozek gallops down the middle and lets fly before Scott can catch him. Trafford sees it all the way, dives to his right to save and gathers the loopy effort from the rebound.

Slama hounds Ngumoha into conceding a corner as the Liverpool winger slips under pressure.

Jude Bellingham is wearing the England captain’s armband again. He was also wearing it during the pre-World Cup camp against New Zealand. Thomas Tuchel explained afterwards that the player with the most caps is skipper when Harry Kane is subbed off. Bellingham is also playing centrally, as a False Nine.

Corner on the right for England who procrastinate so long over their positions the referee warns them but does not take it off them. Krejci and Kane have their arms around each other as the ball comes in and the Czech captain pulls Kane to the ground but the referee waves play on.

Saka takes it short and plays a one-two with Alexander-Arnold. Saka cuts it back to Eze to shoot in a pre-cooked move but he is closed down too quickly so he rolls it to Hall 20 yards out and the left-black leans back and launches his shot 20 rows back behind the goal.

England have a corner on the left after a last gasp tackle by Chaloupek on Gordon.

Although the goal was built from the right, England have been so dominant down the left. Kane takes the ball by the left of the D, spins to wrap his right instep around the ball and try to bend it into the top right corner. Kovar, the PSV goalkeeper, soars to his left to claw it away with his top hand.

Chaloupek is stalking Gordon all over the pitch and Slama is sticking close to Saka. First decent move down the Czech right catches Guehi a little off guard but out comes Trafford to gather.

Yes, for sure [this is as good as I’ve felt in an England shirt. My football IQ, I’m getting better and better, smarter and smarter. I need time to really feel at home, to feel comfortable and once I have that I don’t look back.

[Where do you see this squad in two years?] European champions.

Massively [relishing a run in the No 10 position in place of Bellingham]. I want to try and show what I can do in that role and make a positive impact.

The atmosphere here [is always intense] and they have a new coach. We’ve done our research. We have to respect them. It’s going to be difficult and it’s up to us to hold our nerve.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, said the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”

Trevoh Chalobah will earn his third England cap in tonight’s Nations League match against Czech Republic. The Como centre-back, 27, played in the 6-4 defeat of France in the Bronze final at the World Cup and his other appearance for the Three Lions was in the defeat by Senegal last year.

Trent Alexander-Arnold will make his first England appearance in 15 months after being given a start. The Real Madrid full-back, who was not selected for the World Cup in the summer, earned his last cap against Andorra in 2025.

He replaces Jarell Quansah in Thomas Tuchel’s line-up that lost to Spain at the weekend.

“Trent had a very good training week and the excellent training in Wembley after the match, where he showed that he absolutely wants to play and wants to be with us,” said Tuchel on the eve of the game at Fortuna Arena.

“We’re good. Everything is fine. He’s ready to go. He has qualities that you all know, like he’s strong on the ball, excellent crossing, good finishing. And very, very good on the ball. That’s basically what he brings.”

Ezri Konsa, who missed team training on the day before this game, is out. Morgan Rogers, meanwhile, steps in for Jude Bellingham in the No10 role as Tuchel looks to juggle four matches in 11 days during this extended international break.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is in line to make his first England start under head coach Thomas Tuchel for tonight’s Nations League game against Czech Republic.

Injuries to Nico O’Reilly and Ezri Konsa have forced Tuchel into changes at the back, with Alexander-Arnold expected to come in at right-back, Trevoh Chalobah to replace Konsa and Lewis Hall to step in for O’Reilly.

Alexander-Arnold has made only one appearance under Tuchel, as a substitute in a World Cup qualifying win against Andorra in June 2025. His last start for England came under interim head coach Lee Carsley, when he scored in a victory over Finland.

Jude Belllingham could be given a rest after playing the full 90 minutes in the defeat by Spain, which would give Morgan Rogers an opportunity in the No 10 position.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

#1358. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a big moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso)

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 15:01 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 15:38 EDT, 4 November 2026

FIFA President Gianni Infantino allegedly influenced Trump administration officials to fast-track a work permit for his undocumented Nicaraguan housekeeper after she lost her legal status, according to bombshell documents.

The global soccer chief is alleged to have turned to politically-connected contacts to secure a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez, 33, after the White House revoked her legal permission to work in the United States, according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail.

The Nicaraguan-born Fernandez was reportedly employed by the soccer governing body to work as a housekeeper for the FIFA boss and his family in August 2024. Despite being on FIFA's payroll, she performed no services for the organization.

However, she reportedly continued illegally working in her role and living in the Infantino household for months after the Trump administration terminated the immigration agreement that granted her permission to stay in the United States.

Fernandez is then said to have secured a new work authorization under Kristi Noem's Department of Homeland Security following an intervention by a Trump adviser, documents show.

Infantino allegedly tapped Carlos Cordeiro, the former US Soccer chief who served as a senior World Cup adviser to Donald Trump, to orchestrate the new work permit.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino (right) reportedly enlisted the help of a Trump adviser to secure a work permit for his family's Nicaraguan housekeeper

Infantino allegedly tapped Carlos Cordeiro (pictured) to orchestrate a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez

In January, Infantino reportedly asked Cordeiro, who in May 2025 was appointed to the White House's World Cup task force alongside Noem, to use his connections at the state department to smooth the path to getting Fernandez's new work visa approved, according to the documents.

Cordeiro also allegedly first helped to secure Fernandez's right to work in the US under Infantino's orders in 2024.

Fernandez was reportedly already living and working at Infantino's residence in the millionaires' row of One Thousand Museum in Miami, Florida, where David Beckham recently sold a $25million penthouse, in early 2024.

However, until May 2024, she had not yet filed or received an approved work permit and was therefore working at the residence illegally, per the documents.

During a January 2024 meeting at Infantino's home, Cordeiro, at the FIFA boss's request, is said to have instructed a subordinate to submit their own Miami rental address on Fernandez's immigration filing rather than that of the Infantino family home.

While Fernandez's work visa was initially approved, it came to an abrupt end last year when the Department of Homeland Security terminated the Humanitarian Parole Program for Cuba, Haiti, Venezuela and her native Nicaragua.

On May 30, 2025, the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to scrap the four-country scheme, which had permitted Fernandez and other Nicaraguans to secure permission to work in the US.

Fernandez's contract with FIFA was terminated in October 2025, but she was paid a three-month salary as a bonus and remained illegally working as Infantino's housekeeper for the remainder of the year, according to the documents.

Cordeiro (left) was appointed to Trump's White House's World Cup task force in 2025

Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem worked in connection with the task force

In January 2026, Infantino allegedly asked Cordeiro, who was now working on the World Cup task force which operated directly out of Homeland Security, to leverage his new government contacts to secure Fernandez a new permit.

That same month, Fernandez was granted a new work visa and was re-hired as a FIFA employee on a $40,000-per-year contract until August.

FIFA strongly denied the allegations that it had 'employed an individual in the US without the necessary authorisation.'

'FIFA verifies the employment status of each employee and ensures compliance with U.S. immigration and employment requirements,' a FIFA spokesperson told The Daily Mail.

'Matters related to the FIFA President's personal and home life are private; however, for the avoidance of any doubt, the costs of any domestic staff are met by the FIFA President personally.

The organization added: 'As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.'

Cordeiro did not immediately respond to The Daily Mail's requests for comment.

The Daily Mail also reached out to the DHS for comment and to question why Fernandez was granted a new work permit but did not receive an immediate response.

Infantino, who is standing for reelection in 2027, has faced months of scrutiny

The bombshell report comes after months of scrutiny for Infantino, who faces reelection in 2027.

Infantino faced mutiny earlier this year over his secret plans – later scrapped – to sell a stake in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

It sparked uncertainty around Infantino's future after three confederations rejected his plan, which was then abandoned.

Among them was UEFA, which said it has lost confidence in Infantino and threatened to boycott future World Cups.

Cordeiro also recently quit FIFA over Infantino's commercial deals with Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital.

Infantino faced further scrutiny last month when it was alleged that Infantino personally intervened to suspend USA Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card following a call with President Trump.

In a saga that sparked condemnation from across the world, the striker was originally barred from the USA's last-16 match against Belgium, only for his ban to be sensationally suspended by the FIFA disciplinary committee following a protest by the White House. The New York Post claimed in October that Infantino told Trump in a call on July 1 that 'he would take care of it. One call and it was done.'

FIFA did not comment on the claims at the time but pointed to a July statement from Infantino, when he insisted the decision was made by 'independent' bodies acting 'autonomously.'

Despite mounting pressure over recent months, Infantino intends to stand for a fourth consecutive term next March at the FIFA Congress.

#1356. Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Alterations in the microbial composition of the human gut have been associated with a wide range of chronic diseases1,2. Yet species-level composition alone can obscure extensive within-species genetic diversity and functional variation. This has driven a shift towards strain-resolved, genetic-level analysis of the microbiome, leveraging microbial genetic variation to identify disease-relevant genes and pathways3,4,5,6. Here we conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analysing 12.8 million gut microbial single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with 244 host health phenotypes and environmental exposures in 10,781 individuals from 6 independent cohorts. We identify 940 independent associations across 69 host factors, including age, sex and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters. Structural analyses identified host-phenotype-associated SNVs in functionally important regions of proteins, findings that inform mechanistic hypotheses about how microbial genetic changes relate to environmental and host physiological factors. For example, we identified an age-associated SNV in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that affects an amino acid within the protein pocket that binds glutathione. To support future efforts, all study summary statistics are provided in an online catalogue (https://fulab.web.rug.nl/SNV-MWAS/). Together, these results identify new biological connections between the human host and microbial genetic variants at base pair resolution and provide a resource for hypothesis generation that will aid future understanding of the strain-level functionality of the gut microbiota.

The gut microbiome exhibits large variations in its composition and genetic landscape. Within-species genetic variation underlies strain differences in fitness, metabolic capacities, pathogenicity and other biological properties. Thus, the field of microbiome research is moving towards strain-level or genetic-level dissection of the microbial contributions to human health (Supplementary Information). Structural variations in the gut microbiome have been linked to human body mass index (BMI), bile acid concentrations, the human plasma metabolome and host genetics, thereby identifying bacterial genes involved in glucose metabolism, bile acid biosynthesis and biotransformation, and N-acetylgalactosamine utilization3,4,5,6.

However, gut microbial genomes also contain abundant SNVs that can modulate microbial function and host interactions. For example, a SNV in the blc gene of Escherichia coli disrupts the intestinal barrier by decreasing the amount of lysophosphatidylethanolamine, a metabolite that aids remission of inflammatory bowel disease7. In the stomach, a SNV in Helicobacter pylori increases gastric cancer risk by enhancing the proteolytic activity of the serine protease HtrA (ref. 8). In Bacteroides coprocola, SNVs in glycosyl hydrolase genes have been associated with type 2 diabetes9. A SNV-based metagenome-wide association study (SNV-MWAS) in an Israeli population identified BMI-associated SNVs that were replicated in a geographically independent Dutch cohort10. Despite these examples, systematic explorations of the relationships between gut microbial SNVs and host phenotypes have not, to our knowledge, been carried out at phenome-wide scale. Such analyses require large-scale human cohort data with both metagenomic and deep phenotypic data, and they need to overcome a number of technical challenges. For example, microbial species exhibit complex population genetic structures, and these strong lineage effects may lead to false discoveries in association studies if population structure is not properly controlled.

In this study, we compiled shotgun metagenomic sequencing data of 11,831 faecal samples from 5 independent cohorts from the Netherlands and a cohort from Tanzania. Gut microbial genotypes were characterized using GT-Pro11, yielding 12.8 million SNVs in core genomic regions. We further developed a linear mixed-model (LMM)-based analysis workflow that controls for within-species population genetic structure to ensure that SNV–phenome associations detected are independent from the cumulative effect of strain lineage. We then conducted a PheWAS to identify associations between common metagenomic SNVs and 244 host phenotypic and exposure factors, using LMM in each cohort, followed by meta-analysis. In total, we detected 940 independent association signals supported by multiple cohorts that link 39,663 SNVs across 101 species to 69 host phenotypes or exposures, and the full set of results are available in an online catalogue. We also performed protein structural analyses to interpret the biological relevance of these associations.

We compiled faecal metagenomic sequencing data for 11,831 samples from 10,781 individuals from 6 cohorts (Fig. 1). Five cohorts are from the Netherlands—the Dutch Microbiome Project (DMP; n = 7,955)12, Lifelines-DEEP (LLD; n = 1,135, plus 340 followed up after an average of 4 years (designated LLD1 for baseline samples and LLD2 for follow-up samples))3,13, the 500-Functional Genomics Project (500FG; n = 529)14,15, the 1000 Inflammatory Bowel Disease Project (IBD; n = 544)16 and 300-Obesity (300OB; n = 298)15,17—and one is from Tanzania (300-Tanzania Functional Genomics Project (300TZFG), n = 320)18 (Fig. 1 and Supplementary Table 1). For LLD2 and 500FG, we have additional datasets from some of the same individuals (nLLD2 = 251, nFG500 = 459) with samples processed using both DNA extraction methods19 that allowed us to assess the effect of extraction protocol on SNV profiling and the robustness of microbial genotyping (Fig. 1, Supplementary Table 1 and Supplementary Note 1). The extensive phenotypic information for the corresponding samples was also curated and harmonized. We integrated 244 phenotypic and exposure factors (92 binary and 152 continuous or ordinal traits) available in the DMP or in at least 2 other cohorts for analysis (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Table 2). Among these, 131 phenotypes were available for at least 2 cohorts, whereas 113 were only available for the DMP. Across the whole dataset, the sample size per phenotype ranged from 593 to 11,706 (Supplementary Table 2).

In this study, we integrated whole-genome shotgun sequencing (WGS) data of 11,831 faecal samples from 10,781 individuals from 6 independent cohorts and harmonized 244 phenotype and exposure factors across these cohorts. Two of the six cohorts, Lifelines-DEEP (LLD) and 500-Functional Genomics (500FG), are represented by multiple datasets. n represents the number of faecal samples. LLD contains 1,135 samples collected at the study baseline time point (LLD1) and 340 samples collected for a subset of individuals at a follow-up time point after 4 years that were processed using two DNA isolation kits: 253 by QIAGEN QIAamp Fast DNA Stool Mini Kit (FSK; represented by circled F) (LLD2-FSK) and 338 using QIAGEN AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (APK; represented by circled A) (LLD2-APK). 500FG contains 529 samples that were also processed using the two DNA isolation kits: 517 processed using FSK (500FG-FSK) and 471 processed using APK (500FG-APK). To ensure sample independence in our downstream analysis, we used only LLD1 and 500FG-FSK in this analysis, and the additional datasets (LLD2-FSK, LLD2-APK and 500FG-APK) were used only to carry out technical assessments. We then conducted meta-genotyping for the WGS data from stool samples and generated the gut microbial genotype profile, keeping 12.8 million common biallelic microbial SNVs for the LMM-based SNV-MWAS. SNV-MWAS analyses were conducted separately for the six independent datasets from the six cohorts and then integrated through meta-analysis. Linkage disequilibrium-based grouping was conducted to extract independent signals, and an LMM-based permutation test was used to screen for robust association signals. To provide functional interpretation of SNV associations, we then carried out protein structural analysis. Created in BioRender; Fu, J. https://biorender.com/c1z5z7y (2026).
